We have also continued to provide regular merit-based increases for our employees and are regularly benchmarking our compensation ranges, including share-based compensation, for new and existing employees to ensure we can hire and retain the talent needed to drive growth in our business.

Homecare revenue. Homecare revenue increased by $2,630,000, or 18.6%, for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year. Approximately $1,959,000 of the increase in revenue was due to higher volume, which was driven by additional sales representatives and increased sales representative productivity, and approximately $671,000 was due to higher net revenues per approval. For the nine months ended March 31, 2026, homecare revenue increased by $6,989,000, or 16.7%, compared to the same period in the prior year. Approximately $5,699,000 of the increase in revenue was due to higher volume, which was driven by additional sales representatives and increased sales representative productivity, and approximately $1,290,000 was due to higher net revenues per approval. For the three months ended March 31, 2026, we averaged 57 homecare field sales representatives.

Hospital revenue. Hospital revenue was $1,032,000, an increase of $308,000, or 42.5%, for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year. For the nine months ended March 31, 2026, hospital revenue was $2,734,000, an increase of $597,000, or 27.9%, compared to the same period in the prior year.

gp.heading: Gross profit
gp.text: Gross profit dollars increased to $14,937,000, or 80.0% of net revenues, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $13,197,000, or 78.1% of net revenues, in the same period in the prior year. The increase in gross profit was primarily a result of increased overall revenue and the increase in gross profit percentage was due to revenue mix .

oi.heading: Operating income
oi.text: Operating income increased by $819,000, or 30.7%, to $3,489,000, or 18.7% of net revenues, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year. The increase was primarily due to an increase in revenue and gross profit.

opex.heading: Operating expenses
opex.text:
Selling, general and administrative expenses. Selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses were $11,171,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, representing an increase of $885,000, or 8.6%, compared to the same period in the prior year.

Payroll and compensation-related expenses were $7,413,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, representing an increase of $537,000, or 7.8%, compared to the same period in the prior year. The increase was primarily due to the increase in salaries and incentive compensation related to the higher average number of sales representatives and higher overall compensation costs. We have also continued to provide regular merit-based increases for our employees and are regularly benchmarking our compensation ranges, including share-based compensation, for new and existing employees to ensure we can hire and retain the talent needed to drive growth in our business.

rd.text: Research and development expenses . Research and development (“R&D”) expenses were $277,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, representing an increase of $36,000, or 14.9%, compared to the same period in the prior year. The increase was primarily due to increased average headcount and consulting expenses related to product enhancements and sustaining engineering.

tax.text: Income tax expense was estimated at $876,000, and the effective tax rate was 24.1%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026. Estimated income tax expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026, includes a discrete current tax benefit of $75,000, primarily related to the windfall tax benefit of vested stock awards and vested restricted stock units.

net.heading: Net income
net.text: Net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $2,761,000, representing an increase of 29.3% compared to $2,136,000 for the same period in the prior year. The increase in net income was primarily due to increased revenue and gross profit.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was $373,000. Cash flows provided by operating activities consisted of net income of $2,761,000, non-cash expenses of $701,000, a decrease in income tax receivable, net of $763,000, a decrease in prepaid expenses and other assets of $284,000, and a decrease in contract assets of $68,000. These cash flows from operating activities were offset by a decrease in accrued compensation of $3,241,000, an increase in accounts receivable of $462,000, a decrease in accounts payable and accrued expenses of $347,000, and an increase in inventories of $154,000.

wc.text: Our primary working capital requirements relate to adding employees to our sales force and support functions, continuing infrastructure investments, and supporting general corporate needs, including financing equipment purchases and other capital expenditures incurred in the ordinary course of business. Based on our current operational performance, we believe our working capital of approximately $44,933,000 and available borrowings under our existing credit facility will provide sufficient liquidity to meet our anticipated working capital and other liquidity needs for the next twelve months from the date of this report.

capex.text: Our primary working capital requirements relate to adding employees to our sales force and support functions, continuing infrastructure investments, and supporting general corporate needs, including financing equipment purchases and other capital expenditures incurred in the ordinary course of business. Based on our current operational performance, we believe our working capital of approximately $44,933,000 and available borrowings under our existing credit facility will provide sufficient liquidity to meet our anticipated working capital and other liquidity needs for the next twelve months from the date of this report.

net sales.heading: Net Revenues
net sales.text:
Net revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025 are summarized in the table below.

Homecare revenue. Homecare revenue increased by $2,617,000, or 17.6%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year. The increase in revenue was due to higher volume, which was driven by additional sales representatives and increased sales representative productivity. Throughout the three months ended September 30, 2026, we averaged 63 homecare field sales representatives.

Hospital revenue. Hospital revenue was $716,000, a decrease of $331,000, or 31.6%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year. The decrease in the three months ended September 30, 2026, was primarily due to large capital purchases in the prior period that did not recur, partially offset by an increase in disposable volume.

Homecare distributor revenue. Homecare distributor revenue decreased by $463,000, or 55.9%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year. The decrease in homecare distributor sales was primarily a result of timing of distributor purchases.

Other revenue. Other revenue was $94,000, a decrease of $28,000, or 23.0%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the same period in the prior year.

s.t: Of the $73.4 million of our revenue derived from the U.S. in fiscal 2026, approximately 95.3% represented homecare, inclusive of homecare distributor sales, and 4.7% represented hospital sales.

Collecting a full allowable amount depends on our ability to obtain reimbursement from the patient’s secondary and/or supplemental insurance if the patient has additional coverage, or our ability to collect amounts from individual patients.
We depend on the continued availability and on the levels of state and federal funding, and on the support of state and federal government officials.
We understand that our success and growth depend on attracting, retaining, and developing talent across all levels of the organization.
